name: dmx annotations and dividers
comment: What dmx adds to a Dart file, made visible [editor.dart-highlighting]. Two things a reader needs to see and Dart's own grammar cannot know about: the divider marking the bytes the generator owns, and the single `@dmx` trigger that put them there. `L:` outranks the Dart rules, which is what lets the divider read as a divider rather than as one more `//` comment, and lets the macro name inside `@dmx('model')` read as the macro it names rather than as one more string. `-string` keeps a quoted '@dmx' out of it; a doc comment naming the trigger in prose is deliberately left in.

region-begin.comment: The UNLABELLED divider only. `//#region Helpers` is the author's own fold and dmx never touches it [emission.inline-backend.region-location], so neither does this.
region-begin.name: comment.line.region.begin.dmx

dmx-annotation.comment: The one trigger [surface.annotations]. The macro is a string because it is data, not a type: the name inside the quotes is what generates, so it is scoped as the macro's name while `@dmx` itself is scoped as the annotation.
